businessModel: Bundled free with Quest headsets; supports Meta’s Horizon OS hardware and store business
updateCadence: Every 3–8 weeks in 2026, usually with a Chromium milestone bump every few releases
summary: Meta’s Chromium-based browser for Quest headsets on Horizon OS. It is the main way to run WebXR content on Quest, and it adds spatial features such as wall-anchored windows and tabs inside immersive apps.
bestFor: Quest owners browsing the web or watching video in a headset
WebXR developers testing on real hardware
notFor: People who want a privacy-first or ad-blocking browser
Anyone who needs a desktop-class extension ecosystem

pros.title: WebXR first
pros.detail: WebXR has been on by default since v7.0, with hand and body tracking and WebGPU added later.

pros.title: Spatial windowing
pros.detail: Draggable tabs, wall-anchored windows on Quest 3 and later, and tabs usable inside immersive apps.

pros.title: Modern Chromium
pros.detail: Tracks recent Chromium milestones, so current web apps and sites run.

pros.title: Extensions
pros.detail: Selected extensions have been supported since v32.2 (April 2024).

cons.title: Quest only
cons.detail: Ships on Meta headsets and is not available elsewhere.

cons.title: Closed source
cons.detail: Only the Chromium base is open; Meta’s changes are not.

cons.title: Weak privacy tooling
cons.detail: No built-in tracker or ad blocking documented; telemetry has an opt-out.

faq.q: Is Meta Quest Browser the same as Oculus Browser?
faq.a: Yes. Meta renamed Oculus Browser to Meta Quest Browser in January 2024.

faq.q: Can I use another browser on Quest?
faq.a: Yes, for example Wolvic, which is available from the Meta store and as an APK.

timeline.event: First developer preview of Oculus Browser (codename Carmel)
WebVR removed in v9.0 in favor of WebXR
Version 152.1 adds experimental WebGPU composition layers

switching.note: Password import was added in v36.2; no other importers are documented.

spec.codecs: Chromium codecs; MV-HEVC playback enabled in v150.1
spec.patchLag: Roughly 5–6 weeks behind Chrome by version number

jsSpeed: V8 on a mobile XR chip
smoothness: Windowed in VR; frame rate shared with the system
graphics: WebXR, WebGPU and layers are core features
memory: Headset RAM is shared with the system and apps
cpu: Mobile XR SoC under heavy load
battery: Headset battery drains quickly in any use
securityHardening: Chromium sandbox and site isolation base
patchSpeed: Often a couple of milestones behind Chrome
telemetry: Opt-out exists, tied to a Meta account
lookCustom: Window size and position, few visual options
advancedSettings: Chromium flags reachable on the headset
tabManagement: Draggable tabs, tabs inside immersive apps
devTools: Desktop Chrome DevTools over remote debugging
openSource: Chromium base is open; Meta’s build is not
beginnerFriendly: Works out of the box on Quest

featureNotes.av1: Chromium AV1; hardware path not confirmed
featureNotes.devtools: Remote debugging from a desktop Chrome
